synthesis:
Build plan synthesized below from the verified findings (all confirmed current as of 2026-10-22) and grounded against our existing `arsenal/keylab` toolkit.

---

# Beat-marching pads → chord DB: build plan for Daniel + Vandor

**The one-sentence reality:** Spotify gives you *what's playing and where in the track*, but as of 2024-11-27 it gives a new app **zero** tempo/beat/key data (audio-features & audio-analysis return 403, no replacement 18 months on). So the LED march **cannot** come from Spotify — the beat must be computed locally from captured audio. Good news: every piece needed installs cleanly on Python 3.11 Windows from prebuilt wheels, and our `arsenal/keylab` SysEx toolkit already lights the pads.

---

## 1. NOW-PLAYING + POSITION — recommended path: Windows SMTC (no OAuth)

Read the Spotify **desktop** app's metadata and playback position straight from Windows' System Media Transport Controls. No Spotify account tier, no OAuth, no token refresh.

- **Package:** `winrt-Windows.Media.Control` v3.2.1 (2025-06-06), the modern pywinrt namespaced package — prebuilt cp311 win_amd64 wheels, no compiler. (https://pypi.org/pypi/winrt-Windows.Media.Control/json)
- **Reject:** the old monolithic `winsdk` (frozen 2023, legacy) and the bare `winrt` package (abandoned 2021, Py3.7–3.9 only).
- **API:** `MediaManager.request_async()` → enumerate `get_sessions()`, filter `session.source_app_user_model_id == 'Spotify.exe'` → `try_get_media_properties_async()` for title/artist/album, `get_playback_info().playback_status` for play/pause, `get_timeline_properties()` for `.position` / `.end_time`.
- **Critical behavior:** `position` is a **snapshot** valid only as of `.last_updated_time` (UTC). It does **not** tick on its own. For a smooth progress animation, poll ~1–5 s and extrapolate every frame: `live_pos = position + (now_utc − last_updated_time)` while status == PLAYING; re-sync on `add_timeline_properties_changed`/`add_playback_info_changed` for seeks and pauses. Import namespace is `winrt` (`from winrt.windows.media.control import ...`).

**When to fall back to the Spotify Web API instead:** only if you need the Spotify *web* player (which routes through the browser's SMTC session, not `Spotify.exe`) or metadata when the desktop app isn't the SMTC source. That path needs OAuth Authorization-Code-with-PKCE, a **Premium** app owner, and self-allowlisting (dev mode caps at 5 users in 2026); `GET /me/player/currently-playing` + `progress_ms`/`timestamp`/`duration_ms` still work (https://developer.spotify.com/documentation/web-api/references/changes/february-2026). `spotipy` 2.26.0 (2026-03-03, pure-Python, clean 3.11 install) wraps it. **Default to SMTC** — it's strictly simpler for the solo-desktop case.

---

## 2. BPM / BEAT — recommended path: WASAPI loopback + realtime beat tracker

Since Spotify's beat grid is gone, capture the PC's audio output and run a causal beat tracker on it.

- **Capture:** `PyAudioWPatch` 0.2.12.9 (2026-10-06) — low-latency WASAPI loopback, prebuilt cp311 wheels, `get_default_wasapi_loopback()`. (https://pypi.org/project/PyAudioWPatch/) Alternative block-pull API: `soundcard` 0.4.6 (2026-04-12, pure-Python + cffi). **Not** vanilla `sounddevice`/`pyaudio` — neither does loopback on Windows without a virtual cable.
- **Beat tracker:** `aubio-ledfx` 0.4.12 (2026-10-03) — the LedFx team's maintained aubio fork, prebuilt cp311–3.15 Windows wheels, still imported as `aubio` with the `aubio.tempo` API. (https://pypi.org/project/aubio-ledfx/)
  - **Reject** classic `pip install aubio` — abandoned at 0.4.9 (2019), source-only, no wheels, build-painful on 3.11.
  - **Reject for realtime** madmom (last release 2017, needs old-numpy + Cython + MSVC) and BeatNet (pulls madmom). librosa/`beat_this` are offline/whole-file — use them in the chord phase, not the live loop.

**One-line install:** `py -m pip install PyAudioWPatch aubio-ledfx`

**Realtime loop (standard causal usage):**
```python
tempo = aubio.tempo('default', buf_size, hop_size, samplerate)  # samplerate = 48000!
# each captured block (downmixed to mono):
if tempo(samples):
    fire_pad(); bpm = tempo.get_bpm()
```

---

## 3. PIP INSTALL LIST (we already have librosa/numpy/scipy/requests)

```
py -m pip install "winrt-Windows.Media.Control[all]" PyAudioWPatch aubio-ledfx
```
Optional / later:
- `soundcard` — alternative to PyAudioWPatch if loopback misbehaves.
- `vamphost` — the chord-phase host (section 5); has cp311 win_amd64 wheels.
- `spotipy` — only if you take the Web-API fallback in section 1.

**No MIDI dependency needed** for the LEDs: our `arsenal/keylab` already does SysEx over WinMM via ctypes (no python-rtmidi/mido).

---

## 4. HONEST GOTCHAS

- **Beat-synced LEDs cannot come from Spotify, full stop.** audio-features/audio-analysis died 2024-11-27, return 403 for new apps, no replacement, no waitlist (https://developer.spotify.com/blog/2024-11-27-changes-to-the-web-api). "March to the beat" is the *harder* half; SMTC is the easy half.
- **Loopback captures ALL system audio** — Discord pings, notification dings, a second tab all land in the beat tracker. Expect the lock to wobble when other apps make noise.
- **Samplerate trap:** WASAPI loopback is typically 48000 Hz / 2-ch / float32 shared-mix. You MUST downmix to mono and pass **48000** (not 44100) to `aubio.tempo`, or the BPM is wrong.
- **Realtime lock latency:** ~30–80 ms per beat flag, **a few seconds to lock a stable BPM**, and aubio routinely reports **half/double BPM** — add octave-correction/smoothing if the pads must stay on the right subdivision. (The latency numbers are a reasoned estimate, not a hard benchmark — measure on the rig.)
- **Silence handling:** loopback yields silent/no-data frames when nothing plays — guard the loop so it doesn't stall or lock onto noise.
- **SMTC position is a snapshot** (section 1) — extrapolate or the progress bar jumps.
- **Install audit noise (benign):** winrt-runtime/Media.Control show a "files added late" PyPI notice (3.14 wheels uploaded 2025-09-20) — maintainer adding 3.14 support, not a compromise.
- **aubio-ledfx caveat:** clean install + standard `aubio.tempo` are confirmed; its PyPI page does **not** document the "reduced-latency/multi-octave" improvements some sources attribute to it — treat those as unverified.

---

## 5. CHORD PHASE — realistic path to a time-synced chord DB

**Architecture: analyze once, replay in sync.** Do NOT run a chord model on short live buffers (inaccurate, high latency). Instead:

1. **Offline per track:** capture or load the audio, run **Chordino (NNLS-Chroma)** to get `(start, end, chord)` labels. Host: `vamphost` (cp311 win_amd64 wheels, latest 1.4.0 2026-10-07 — https://pypi.org/pypi/vamphost/json). **Caveat:** pip gives you the *engine only* — you must separately drop the Chordino/NNLS-Chroma plugin DLL into `C:\Program Files\Vamp Plugins` (or set `VAMP_PATH`); the model is a free download from vamp-plugins.org / isophonics.net.
2. **Store** `(track_id, time, chord)` rows in our own DB (fits the Akasha append-only substrate).
3. **Replay:** sync stored `(time, chord)` to the live position from SMTC (section 1) — the LEDs change color on chord changes in time with the music.

**Accuracy expectations:** Chordino is older-gen (~mid-70s% maj/min, weaker on 7ths/inversions) — fine for "march the pads to the chord," weak for a precise sheet. Higher accuracy = modern PyTorch chord models (BTC transformer / ChordMini family; torch has clean cp311 wheels, you supply weights) — **but** ChordMini's pipeline drags in madmom's Windows build pain; budget WSL/Linux or a torch-only model that avoids madmom.

**Seeding / why Ultimate Guitar won't directly feed it:**
- **Ultimate Guitar:** no sanctioned API; only brittle ToS-violating scrapers, and its sheets are chord-over-lyric **text with no timestamps** — unusable as `(track,time,chord)` directly. Useful at most as a chord-vocabulary/validation hint.
- **Chordify:** has time-synced chords but closed, ToS forbids automated access.
- **AcousticBrainz:** dead (submissions ended 2022).
- **Academic sets (Isophonics/Beatles, McGill Billboard, RWC-Pop):** time-aligned annotations but no audio and tiny fixed song lists — use to **validate** our extractor, not to populate it.

Bottom line: there is **no legal time-synced chord feed to pull at scale** — we generate the DB ourselves with Chordino/torch over audio we have, and use the external sources only for validation and chord-name hints.

---

## 6. MVP SLICE — smallest thing that makes the pads march

We already own the output layer — **`arsenal/keylab`** (SysEx over WinMM, no deps):
- `py -m arsenal.keylab connect` arms DAW mode (gates the LEDs).
- `pad <1..12> <colour>`, `led`, `all`, `rainbow`, `chord <spec>` light the RGB pads; `bench --hz` already measured the colour-update ceiling.
- Wire format in `arsenal/keylab/protocol.py` (byte-builders, testable, read from Arturia's own FL integration script); I/O in `winmidi.py`.

**MVP (one evening):**
1. `py -m pip install PyAudioWPatch aubio-ledfx`
2. `py -m arsenal.keylab connect` (close FL first so it isn't fighting for the DAW port).
3. Small script: PyAudioWPatch loopback → downmix mono @48000 → `aubio.tempo` → **on each beat flag, advance a color/pad cursor** by calling into `arsenal.keylab.protocol` builders (reuse the `pad`/`led` SysEx path directly rather than shelling out per beat, to stay inside the LedStrip queue's rate ceiling). Colors can cycle a palette per beat, or map BPM→hue.
4. Confirm against `bench` findings that per-beat sends stay under the visible-stall rate.

That alone gives "pads march to the beat, changing color as it clicks through." **Layer 2** adds SMTC (section 1) for a position-driven progress animation. **Layer 3** adds the offline Chordino DB (section 5) so pad colors follow chord changes.

**Pre-flight checks before building:** confirm the KeyLab enumerates as `KeyLab 88 mk3 DAW` (`py -m arsenal.keylab ports`); if you take the Spotify Web-API fallback, confirm Daniel's account is Premium (dead app otherwise).

---

**Key files referenced (all absolute):** `E:\AI-Setup\arsenal\keylab\README.md`, `E:\AI-Setup\arsenal\keylab\protocol.py`, `E:\AI-Setup\arsenal\keylab\winmidi.py`, `E:\AI-Setup\arsenal\keylab\__main__.py`, `E:\AI-Setup\arsenal\midiports.py`.

verified.front: Spotify Web API — current (2026) state: you CAN get now-playing + track position in realtime, but you CANNOT get BPM/beat-grid/key from Spotify for any new app. Player-read endpoints (GET /me/player, GET /me/player/currently-playing) survived the Feb/March 2026 endpoint purge and still return is_playing, progress_ms, timestamp and item.duration_ms — enough to drive a realtime position animation. But the only Spotify source of tempo/beat-grid/key (GET /audio-features, GET /audio-analysis) has been deprecated since 2024-11-27, returns 403 for any app without a pre-existing quota extension, still carries a "Deprecated" banner in 2026, and has NO official replacement 18 months on. CONSEQUENCE for the LED-march goal: beat-synced lights cannot come from Spotify — BPM/beats must come from local audio capture (WASAPI loopback) + a realtime beat tracker (librosa/aubio/madmom/Essentia), or a fuzzy third-party per-track BPM lookup (single number, no in-time grid). VERDICT: front confirmed current as of 2026-10-22.

verified.claim: GET /me/player (Get Playback State) and GET /me/player/currently-playing (Get Currently Playing Track) are STILL AVAILABLE in 2026 — explicitly listed under 'Player' in the 'still available' section of the official Feb 2026 changelog; they survived the Feb/March 2026 endpoint removals (which killed ~15 catalog/profile/'Get Several' endpoints).

currently-playing needs scope user-read-currently-playing; full playback state (/me/player) needs user-read-playback-state. Response gives is_playing, progress_ms, timestamp and item.duration_ms — enough to interpolate realtime track position — but NOT tempo/beat/key.

OAuth: Authorization Code with PKCE is the officially recommended flow for desktop/native apps (no client secret stored); access tokens are short-lived (~1h) and refreshed via the refresh token. A long-running LED app must handle token refresh (proactively and on 401).

DEPRECATED/BROKEN for new apps: GET /audio-features and GET /audio-analysis (the ONLY Spotify source of tempo/BPM, beat grid and key) were deprecated 2024-11-27 and return HTTP 403 for any app created — or without a pending quota extension — after that date. The endpoint docs still show a 'Deprecated' banner in 2026. Same-day casualties: recommendations, related-artists, featured-playlists.

As of mid-2026 there is STILL NO official Spotify replacement for tempo/BPM/beat/key — no waitlist, no public statement. No third-party service reproduces a BEAT GRID (per-beat timestamps); alternatives (GetSongBPM, AcousticBrainz, ReccoBeats, Essentia, etc.) give at most a single BPM number with fuzzy track matching. Reproducing the old beat grid requires running a beat tracker on the audio yourself.

A brand-new dev app CAN read the owner's currently-playing, but 2026 Development Mode is tightened: max 5 allowlisted users (down from 25) AND the app OWNER must have a Spotify Premium account. Non-allowlisted users get 403. For solo/own-playback use this is fine (allowlist yourself, hold Premium).

Extended Quota Mode is NOT obtainable by an individual: since 2025-05-15 Spotify only accepts applications from organizations (registered business entity, launched service with 250k+ MAU, key-market availability, up to 6-week review). A solo hobby project will never qualify — but does not NEED extended quota for personal single-user use.

July 2026 quota update: client IDs raised to 25 per developer account, but quota is now SHARED per developer account across all dev-mode client IDs (splitting work across apps buys no extra budget); it did NOT raise the 5-user cap or grant extended quota. 429 bodies now include reason:'QUOTA_EXCEEDED'.

Python client: spotipy is the standard Web API wrapper, installs cleanly on Python 3.11 Windows (pure-Python, pip wheel, no compiled/native build; core deps requests/urllib3; memcache is an optional extra). Latest 2.26.0 released 2026-03-03 — after the Feb 2026 migration, so it tracks the renamed/removed endpoints. It cannot restore the dead audio-features/analysis endpoints (calling them just surfaces Spotify's 403).

gotchas: Beat-synced LEDs CANNOT come from Spotify in 2026. Spotify gives you position (progress_ms) but zero tempo/beat/key for a new app. The LED march-to-the-beat must be driven by a LOCAL realtime beat tracker, not the Web API.

progress_ms is a snapshot, not a live clock. To animate smoothly you must interpolate: position_now = progress_ms + (wall_clock_now - timestamp) while is_playing, and only re-poll /me/player every ~1-5s (polling tighter risks the 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED). There is no push/websocket for playback position — you poll.

The app OWNER must have Spotify Premium for a dev-mode app to function at all, and you must add yourself to the 5-user allowlist. Free-tier owner = dead app. Confirm Daniel's account is Premium before building.

Access tokens expire ~1h. A long-running LED daemon MUST refresh proactively (and retry once on 401) or it goes dark mid-session. spotipy's SpotifyPKCE auth manager handles this if you persist the token cache.

For the realtime BPM/beat grid: capture system audio via WASAPI loopback (soundcard or pyaudiowpatch on Windows — NOT vanilla pyaudio, which lacks loopback). Then run a realtime beat tracker. librosa installs cleanly (numpy/scipy/soundfile wheels) but is batch-oriented, not truly realtime; aubio is lighter and streaming-friendly but its PyPI wheels have been flaky on Py3.11/Windows (may need a build or a prebuilt wheel) — VERIFY aubio installs before committing to it. madmom/Essentia are heavier builds on Windows — budget for build pain.

The ultimatechords/own-chord-DB endgame depends ENTIRELY on local audio analysis (chroma + chord recognition on the captured waveform), because Spotify will never hand you key/chord data. Architect the pipeline around local DSP from day one; treat Spotify purely as the 'what track + where in it' metadata source.

Third-party BPM lookups (GetSongBPM, ReccoBeats, AcousticBrainz) return ONE BPM number per track via fuzzy title/artist matching — no per-beat timestamps and no in-time grid, so they cannot drive a marching animation even as a fallback. Useful only as a tempo hint.

spotipy full-compatibility caveat is now resolved: 2.26.0 shipped 2026-03-03, right after the Feb 2026 migration, so it reflects the endpoint renames. If anything behaves oddly, confirm the installed version is >= 2.26.0 (older pinned versions predate the migration).

verified.front: win-nowplaying — VERIFIED, holds up as of 2026-10-22. Reading "now playing + position" for the Spotify desktop app on Windows/Python 3.11 via SMTC (Windows.Media.Control) is the right, OAuth-free front, and every package and behavior claim in it checks out against current (2025/2026) sources. Install `winrt-Windows.Media.Control[all]` (v3.2.1, 2025-06-06) — the modern pywinrt namespaced package, prebuilt cp311 win_amd64 wheels, no compiler; it hard-depends on winrt-runtime~=3.2.1.0 and the [all] extra pulls winrt-Windows.Foundation/Foundation.Collections/Media/Storage.Streams (all ~=3.2.1). The old monolithic `winsdk` (1.0.0b10, 2023-08) still imports on 3.11 but is frozen/legacy; the bare `winrt` package (1.0.21033.1, 2021-02) is abandoned — reject it. SMTC delivers title/artist/album, play/pause status, and a timeline position that is a SNAPSHOT valid only as of last_updated_time — it must be polled and extrapolated for smooth per-frame LED motion. The hard ceiling to flag up front: SMTC never exposes BPM/tempo/beats/chords, and Spotify's audio-features/audio-analysis API (the classic BPM + beat-grid source) was cut off for new apps on 2024-11-27 with no replacement, so realtime tempo and the eventual chord-DB are an entirely separate workstream (local WASAPI loopback + librosa/aubio/madmom, or a third-party service).

verified.claim: The current package for SMTC is the pywinrt namespaced winrt-Windows.Media.Control; latest v3.2.1 (2025-06-06), requires_python >=3.9, ships a prebuilt cp311 win_amd64 wheel, and hard-depends on winrt-runtime~=3.2.1.0. The [all] extra pulls winrt-Windows.Foundation, Foundation.Collections, Media, and Storage.Streams (all ~=3.2.1). Install with pip install "winrt-Windows.Media.Control[all]"; no compiler needed.
winrt-runtime is a compiled extension but ships a prebuilt cp311 win_amd64 wheel (v3.2.1, 2025-06-06, ~242 kB) — no local C++ build required on Python 3.11 Windows.

The old monolithic winsdk package is frozen at 1.0.0b10 (2023-08-11, pre-release) — it still imports on Python 3.8-3.12 (from winsdk.windows.media.control import ...) but is legacy/superseded by the namespaced packages; usable only as a fallback, not the thing to build on.
The bare 'winrt' PyPI package is Microsoft's abandoned original — last release 1.0.21033.1 on 2021-02-03, labeled Beta, targets only Python 3.7-3.9, never updated for modern projection. Do NOT use.

SMTC reads title/artist/album and play/pause status with no OAuth: MediaManager.request_async() then try_get_media_properties_async() -> .title/.artist/.album_title and get_playback_info().playback_status; pywinrt projects WinRT PascalCase to snake_case.

Timeline position is a SNAPSHOT, not a live clock: get_timeline_properties().position (timedelta) is valid only as of .last_updated_time (UTC); .end_time gives length. For smooth per-beat LED motion you must poll (~30-60 Hz) and extrapolate live_pos = position + (now_utc - last_updated_time) while playing; a last_updated_time stuck at the 1601 sentinel means the app publishes no position.

The Spotify DESKTOP app integrates with SMTC and reports metadata, play/pause status, and timeline position/duration; filter multiple players by session.source_app_user_model_id ('Spotify.exe'); the Spotify WEB player instead routes through the browser's SMTC session. (Desktop integration confirmed; the specific '~4.5 s republish interval' detail comes from a single third-party GitHub source and is not independently verifiable.)

SMTC exposes no BPM/tempo/beats/chords, and Spotify's audio-features/audio-analysis API (the classic BPM + beat-grid source) was cut off for apps created after 2024-11-27 (403, no waitlist, no public path forward). Realtime tempo for this project must come from local audio analysis (WASAPI loopback -> librosa/aubio/madmom) or a third-party service; the chord-change DB is a further, separate workstream.

gotchas: Position does not tick on its own. get_timeline_properties().position is frozen at its last_updated_time; relying on timeline-changed events alone gives coarse, jumpy motion. Run your own ~30-60 Hz poll loop and extrapolate (pos + (now_utc - last_updated_time)) while status == PLAYING, and re-sync on add_timeline_properties_changed / add_playback_info_changed for seeks and pauses.

Top-level import namespace is winrt (not winsdk). With the namespaced packages you write 'from winrt.windows.media.control import ...'; the winsdk-era 'from winsdk.windows...' path only applies to the legacy package.

Do not call get_current_session() blindly if more than one app can play. It can return the browser, a game, or another player. Enumerate mgr.get_sessions() and filter by source_app_user_model_id == 'Spotify.exe'. Note that listening via Spotify's WEB player makes the source the browser's AUMID, not Spotify.exe, so this front only covers the desktop app.

PyPI flags a benign 'files added late' notice on both winrt-runtime and winrt-Windows.Media.Control: three CPython 3.14 wheels were uploaded 2025-09-20, over three months after the 2025-06-06 release. This is the maintainer adding 3.14 support, not a compromise, but it is the kind of warning that can spook an automated install audit.

The '~4.5 s Spotify republish interval' in the front is from one third-party GitHub project, not an official source. The direction (Spotify republishes periodically + immediately on events) is sound and is exactly why extrapolation is required, but do not treat 4.5 s as a guaranteed constant — measure it at runtime.

The whole BPM/beat/chord goal is NOT reachable through this front or through the Spotify API anymore. Spotify killed audio-features/audio-analysis for new apps on 2024-11-27 with no replacement 18+ months on. Budget realtime tempo as a genuinely separate build (WASAPI loopback capture into librosa/aubio/madmom beat tracking, or a third-party service like ReccoBeats), and the timed chord-change DB as a third layer beyond that. Set expectations: 'march to the beat' is the harder half, not the SMTC half.

winrt-runtime is a compiled C-extension; it only runs cleanly on Python 3.11 because a prebuilt cp311 wheel exists. If the environment ever drifts to a Python with no matching wheel (e.g. a brand-new minor before wheels ship), pip would attempt a source build and likely fail. The 3.11 pin in this project's Python-version strategy is exactly what keeps this clean.

verified.claim: PyAudioWPatch is the best low-latency WASAPI loopback capture lib on Python 3.11 Windows and installs cleanly from prebuilt wheels (no compiler). Latest 0.2.12.9 released 2026-10-06, wheels for CPython 3.9-3.15 incl. 3.11/3.12/3.13, WASAPI loopback via get_default_wasapi_loopback()/get_wasapi_loopback_analogue_by_index(). Note: it is MORE current than the finding stated (finding said ~0.2.12.x Jan 2025; actual latest is Oct 2026).

soundcard does native WASAPI loopback on Windows and installs cleanly (pure Python + cffi, no build). Latest 0.4.6 released 2026-04-12; loopback support present since 2018. Good block-pull alternative to PyAudioWPatch.

Plain python-sounddevice is NOT a loopback tool: WasapiSettings still exposes only exclusive, auto_convert, and explicit_sample_format -- no loopback flag (docs confirm, latest release 0.5.6, 2026-08-17). It installs cleanly on 3.11 but cannot capture speaker output without a fork or virtual cable.

The classic `pip install aubio` is abandoned and build-painful on 3.11 Windows: last release 0.4.9 is from 2019-02-08, source-only tar.gz with no wheels. Do not use it; the algorithm is fine but the packaging is the blocker.

aubio-ledfx is the realtime beat/tempo pick: maintained fork by the LedFx team, `pip install aubio-ledfx` with prebuilt Windows wheels for CPython 3.11-3.15, still imported as `aubio` with the aubio.tempo API. Latest 0.4.12 released 2026-10-03. (The install and maintained status are confirmed; the fork's specific 'realtime tempo improvements' are not documented on its PyPI page -- see gotchas.)

madmom is the most accurate classical tracker but inactive and painful on 3.11: last release 0.16.1 dates to 2017-11-14 (finding said 2018 -- actually 2017), no updates since, and it breaks on modern numpy/Python 3.10+ without old-numpy pins + Cython + a C compiler.

BeatNet (latest 1.1.3, 2023-11-28) inherits madmom's install pain: its setup.py install_requires lists madmom>=0.16.1 (plus librosa, torch, etc.), so it cannot install cleanly on 3.11 Windows without first solving madmom.

beat_this (CPJKU, ISMIR 2024, 'Beat This! Accurate Beat Tracking Without DBN Postprocessing') installs cleanly where PyTorch wheels exist -- madmom is OPTIONAL (only for --dbn postprocessing) -- but it is offline whole-file only, no streaming/realtime API. Ideal for the eventual chord/beat-over-time DB, not live LEDs.
librosa.beat.beat_track installs cleanly on 3.11 Windows but is offline-oriented; not suited to sub-100ms live LED sync. Use it for after-the-fact tempo/beat extraction.

Minimal realtime loop is correct: tempo = aubio.tempo('default', buf_size, hop_size, samplerate); each captured block -> is_beat = tempo(samples); if is_beat: fire pad and read tempo.get_bpm(). Standard causal aubio.tempo usage.

Honest realtime latency with aubio.tempo: ~30-80ms end-to-end beat flag, a few seconds to lock a stable BPM, occasional half/double-BPM. Plausible from the causal design and hop sizing, but this is a reasoned estimate, not a hard 2026 benchmark -- measure on the actual rig.

CRITICAL for the broader Spotify goal: Spotify deprecated audio_features (BPM) and audio_analysis (beat grid) on 2024-11-27; new/dev-mode apps without a pre-deadline quota extension get 403, and ~18 months on there is still no official replacement. You can still read what is playing + track position via the Web API, but you CANNOT get BPM/beats from Spotify -- which is exactly why the loopback+analysis route is the right approach.

gotchas: Spotify can no longer give you BPM or a beat grid: the audio_features and audio_analysis endpoints were deprecated 2024-11-27 and new apps get 403. The Web API still returns now-playing track + playback position, so use Spotify only for 'what's playing / where in the track', and get tempo/beats from WASAPI loopback + a local analyzer.
WASAPI loopback on Windows is typically 48000 Hz, 2-channel, float32, shared-mode mix. You MUST downmix to mono and pass the real samplerate (48000, not 44100) to aubio.tempo, or BPM will be wrong.

WASAPI loopback delivers silence / 'no data' when nothing is playing. Handle it: PyAudioWPatch yields silent frames; soundcard needed its PR #167 fix (synthesize zeros after ~50ms) to avoid stalling on silence-at-start.

aubio-ledfx's PyPI page confirms it is a maintained fork with clean 3.11-3.15 wheels and the aubio.tempo API, but does NOT document the specific 'dynamic/multi-octave/reduced-latency' realtime improvements the finding attributed to it -- treat those accuracy claims as unverified; what's proven is the clean install + the standard aubio.tempo behavior.
aubio.tempo routinely reports half- or double-BPM and needs a few seconds of steady beat to lock. Expect it; add octave-correction / smoothing if the LEDs must stay on the right subdivision.

madmom (last release 2017-11-14) and therefore BeatNet (requires madmom>=0.16.1 in setup.py) will NOT pip-install cleanly on Python 3.11 Windows -- they need an old-numpy pin, Cython, and a C compiler. The highest-accuracy live trackers are the ones with the worst install story here.

Split the stack by job: live LEDs = PyAudioWPatch (or soundcard) + aubio-ledfx; the eventual chord/beat-over-time DB = beat_this or librosa run offline over recorded tracks. beat_this, librosa, and classic aubio are all offline/build-constrained and wrong for the realtime loop.

Out of scope of this audio research but worth flagging for the actual goal: lighting the Arturia KeyLab mk3 RGB pads is a separate MIDI/SysEx output problem (python-rtmidi / mido), not part of this capture+beat stack. The verified work here produces the beat flag and BPM (the input); mapping that to pad colors is a distinct output layer still to be built/verified.

verified.claim: Chordino (NNLS-Chroma) Vamp plugin via the Python vamp/vamphost package is the cleanest working Windows+Python 3.11 chord path and ships prebuilt cp311 win_amd64 wheels, giving time-synced chord labels.

madmom does NOT install cleanly on Python 3.11: the only PyPI release (0.16.1, 2018) is broken on Python 3.10+ (collections.MutableSequence import); the git main 0.17.dev0 fixes it but is a from-source Cython/MSVC build on Windows.

autochord explicitly does NOT support Windows; it is a 2021 ISMIR demo (tested Ubuntu 18.04 only), runs NNLS-Chroma for chroma + a TensorFlow Bi-LSTM-CRF, outputs (start,end,chord) / .lab, and is inactive.

essentia (has a ChordsDetection algorithm) has NO Windows Python bindings; its own docs say 'Python bindings are not supported yet' on Windows, so it cannot be pip-installed for native Windows Python 3.11 use (WSL2/Docker only).

chord-extractor (wraps Chordino, outputs ChordChange(chord, timestamp)) is Linux-first: its compiled Chordino binary defaults to Linux 64-bit; other OSes must install the Vamp plugin pack and set VAMP_PATH, plus libsndfile - not a clean Windows install.

For higher accuracy, modern PyTorch deep chord models (BTC transformer / chord-CNN, e.g. the ChordMini family) are the current route and torch has clean cp311 Windows wheels, but you supply the model weights.

Realtime chord recognition is materially harder and less accurate than offline; near-realtime (1-3 s rolling buffer, ~1-2 s latency) is feasible but frame-accurate live chords are not a solved, accurate thing.

Spotify is NOT a source of chords, BPM, or audio: Get Audio Features and Get Audio Analysis were deprecated for new apps on 27 Nov 2024 (still in force 2026), and Spotify never exposes raw audio; currently-playing track + progress_ms (position) remain available.

To analyze what Spotify is playing you must capture the PC's audio output via WASAPI loopback (e.g. PyAudioWPatch or soundcard); PyAudioWPatch is actively maintained and pip-installs with cp311 Windows wheels.

Ultimate Guitar has NO sanctioned public API; only unofficial reverse-engineered mobile-API scrapers exist (ToS-violating, brittle), and its chord sheets are chord-over-lyric text with no per-chord timestamps - unusable directly for a (track,time,chord) DB.

Chordify produces time-synced chords but is a closed product with no public developer API, and its Terms forbid automated access/scraping (bots, spiders, scrapers) without express written permission, personal non-commercial use only.

AcousticBrainz shut down: submissions ended June 2022 and the live API went offline after the 16 Feb 2022 announcement; only the one-time static data dumps remain (and its data was low-level descriptors, not time-synced chords).

gotchas: NEW 2026 Spotify squeeze not in the original findings: beyond the Nov-2024 audio-features/analysis death, Spotify tightened developer ('dev mode') access again in Feb 2026 - new integrations now require a Premium account and test-user limits, with a migration dated ~Feb 11 / Mar 9 2026. Plan for Premium + OAuth even just to read currently-playing / progress_ms. (TechCrunch 2026-02-06; rspotify issue #550)

The one PyPI-fetch that said vamphost has 'no Windows wheels' was WRONG - the raw JSON (pypi.org/pypi/vamphost/json) shows cp311 win_amd64 wheels for 1.2.1 through 1.4.0 (latest 1.4.0, 2026-10-07, requires_python >=3.10). Verify library claims against the JSON/files API, not a prose scrape.

vamphost is only the HOST - you still must separately install the Chordino / NNLS-Chroma plugin DLL into C:\Program Files\Vamp Plugins (or set VAMP_PATH). pip gives you the engine, not the plugin; the chord model is a separate free download from vamp-plugins.org / isophonics.net.

Chordino accuracy is older-generation (~mid-70s% maj/min WCSR, worse on 7ths/inversions/bass, ~50-70%). It is reliable and fully offline but will mislabel extended chords - fine for 'march the LEDs to the chord', weak for a precise chord DB.

Architecture: do the chord analysis ONCE offline per track into the DB, then on replay sync stored (time,chord) to Spotify's reported progress_ms. Do not try to run Chordino/madmom on short live buffers - that is the inaccurate, high-latency path. BPM/beat grid likewise must be computed locally (librosa/madmom) from loopback, since Spotify no longer gives tempo.

Academic ground-truth datasets (Isophonics/Beatles, McGill Billboard, RWC-Pop) DO give time-aligned chord annotations but ship NO audio and cover a fixed small song set - they are for VALIDATION of your extractor, not for coverage. Hooktheory (~70k songs) is beat-relative, not audio-second, and behind an account. There is no legal, sanctioned, time-synced chord feed to pull at scale (this part of the findings list was truncated but matches what was verifiable).

ChordMini runs its backend on Python 3.10.x and leans on madmom for beat tracking - so the 'modern PyTorch route' still drags in the madmom build pain on Windows. Budget for either WSL/Linux for the deep models or a torch-only chord model that avoids madmom. The arXiv id cited in the finding (2512.22621) was not independently confirmed; the ChordMiniApp repo and its models are confirmed active.

madmom's realistic Windows install is 'pip install git+https://github.com/CPJKU/madmom.git' which needs Cython + MSVC Build Tools and still has reported numpy-float/Windows build snags - not a wheel. Do not promise a clean pip install.

torch itself installs clean on cp311 Windows, but confirm the exact cp311 wheel for your CUDA/CPU build via the official --index-url (download.pytorch.org); PyPI's default is CPU-only and newest releases chase the newest Python first.
